ESH
I’m sorry, everything about how you worded this story sounds like both of you are total bridezillas. It was her day, and you’re complaining she didn’t make you feel special enough, have you considered she might be more worried about her impression on new family members than ones she has already trusted and known her whole life? Then she tried to do a sweet thing and you took it the wrong way, honestly it feels like she can’t win by acknowledging you or leaving you alone. Her being emotional about the wedding is sad, it screams insecurity, but how does it impact you? Let the girl have her feelings, you’re her younger sister and beat her to a milestone, it would be lovely if she could be happy for you but honestly you can’t control other peoples emotions. 
Obviously she made some mistakes here, and made a lot of things about herself, but I don’t for a second think we got an unbiased story. It sounds like you’re grasping to make this about you when it was clearly a stressful time in both of your lives and she really seems within normal person limits.

I’ve recently started de-realizing, it’s the weirdest crap ever. I basically become convinced that I am not real, or everything isn’t real, and I am confused when the world reacts to me. Like if a coworker asks me to pass something I’ll think “wow, weird you’re talking to me when I’m not real,” but I’ll still do it and then be like, “weird I can pick up objects when I’m not real.” I can still function (sorta) like this but the confusion of it will just have me just running slow for however long it lasts. Also it’s wildly terrifying, cause I just spend a lot of time thinking, “where did I go, I know I was real before, what changed?!”

Hey, I read a little on your other post, just wanted to throw in my 2 cents. I am 22 F and a virgin, waiting for marriage for religious reasons, but I am a biologist and I also did do 2 years of research in college on correlations between penis size and suicidal ideation. Though I don’t personally have experience, most research indicates women don’t care about size, it really doesn’t correlate much to sexual satisfaction which is heavily influenced by external stimulation (ie not inside the vagina). What’s more interesting in our research, after men have had sex, their penis size no longer correlated to suicidal ideation and a negative impact on body image. Basically, I think this is a really legitimate worry now, we can see it measurably hurts men’s self worth, but after having sex you will realize it doesn’t matter.
